title: Messier 83: central region
caption: The central region of the spiral galaxy Messier 83, imaged by ESO's Very Large Telescope
celestial: M 83, Messier 83, NGC 5236 · constellation Hydra · about 15 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: This view shows the central region of Messier 83, a spiral galaxy also known as NGC 5236, about 15 million light-years away in the southern constellation Hydra, the Water-Snake. It was made with the FORS1 instrument on the VLT's ANTU telescope by overlaying three frames taken through different filters.
Its spiral pattern resembles that of our own Milky Way, but M83 also has a bar-like structure at its centre. In a barred spiral, the arms reach out from the ends of such a bar of stars.

The three frames were taken through blue, red and near-infrared filters and shown as blue, green and red. All three are available from the ESO Science Data Archive. The field covers about 6.8 by 6.8 arcminutes, recorded in frames of 2048 by 2048 pixels, with the atmosphere blurring the view by about 0.8 arcseconds on average.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (6.45 x 6.82 arcminutes) and distance (15 million light years), the frame spans roughly 28,000 × 30,000 light-years. Its light set out about 15 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: FORS1 recorded blue light (B, shown blue), red light (R, shown green) and near-infrared light (I, shown red).
